title: Industrial Engineering, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College -- a genuinely separate curriculum from University Park's Industrial Engineering, B.S. (IE-2026.json), confirmed by direct bulletin comparison 2026-08-27: Behrend's third/fourth-year required set (IE 302, 305, 322, 327, 405, 311/307, 323, 460, 418, 425, 470, 330, 453, 480W) diverges substantially from UP's own (IE 312, 322 [as an 'engineering elective' pick, not required], 330, 405, 425, 453, 460, 480W plus a Manufacturing Process/Human Factors elective structure) -- Behrend runs its own ABET-accredited industrial engineering curriculum sharing only about half its required courses with UP's General Option. Built fresh (Pattern B) as IEBH per this session's new-major-code convention (UP code IE + 'BH'). Real 8-semester Suggested Academic Plan, 130 total credits, taken verbatim from the live 2026-27 Behrend bulletin page. 'Engineering Elective' (x2) and 'Science Elective' (Second Year Spring) have NO enumerated course list on Behrend's own bulletin page -- its own footnote literally reads 'Ask department for list' -- modeled as plain generic slots, honestly undocumented rather than fabricated (same convention as ME-2026's own generic Engineering/General Technical Elective pools when no list was published). 'IE Specialization Course' (1cr, Fourth Year Fall) is wired to the bulletin's own explicit recommendation, IE 497 (footnoted 'FALL SEMESTER ONLY'). 'IE Technical Elective' (x2) is wired via match to any real IE course not already required elsewhere in this plan, per the bulletin's own footnote 'Must be an IE course' (the co-op/internship/ROTC alternate paths it also mentions aren't course codes and aren't modeled, same documented gap as UP IE-2026's own Engineering elective notes). Real-prereq-chain fix (same pattern as IE-2026): CHEM 110 -> MATH 22 -> MATH 21, none natively in this plan; added MATH 21 + MATH 22 (Semester 1) so CHEM 110 (Semester 1 on the real bulletin) actually unlocks.
